client_assessments.rationale: PMID30536958: The recorded experiments place RARA in chaperone machinery or regulation of HSP90/another substrate; they do not demonstrate that RARA is the chaperoned substrate. Recorded result: The zinc-inducible PML/RARA fusion reduced HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 transcripts and broad HSP90 protein in U937-PR9 cells but not zinc-treated mock controls. Broad HSP90 immunoblots do not separate alpha from beta protein, although both transcripts and promoter regions are resolved.

To establish candidacy, additional source results would need a controlled protein-specific folding, maturation, maintenance, productive-assembly or competence response linked to HSP90; association, RNA/pathway response or machinery membership alone is insufficient.

summary: In human T24 and TCCSUP bladder-cancer cells, anti-HSP90AB1 immunoprecipitation recovered LRP5, and HSP90AB1 overexpression reduced LRP5 ubiquitination, increased LRP5 abundance, activated β-catenin signaling, and rescued alantolactone-suppressed malignant phenotypes. client_assessments.rationale: PMID22195965: This source is currently marked for source recheck and cannot nominate a client. Retained result: In human cells, NASP depletion reduced the soluble H3-H4 reservoir. Figure 6C shows that isoform-specific depletion of HSP90AB1/HSP90 beta, using an siRNA directed to NM_007355.2, rescued soluble H3-H4 loss caused by NASP depletion; Hsc70 depletion produced a related rescue, and LAMP2A experiments implicated chaperone-mediated autophagy. The authors report that HSP90 alpha depletion did not increase soluble histones, although that negative result is not shown. These current data support beta-resolved functional epistasis in a NASP-histone-quality-control pathway, but do not demonstrate NASP-HSP90 binding, co-complex membership, or client status.
limitations: Crosslinking and affinity copurification do not establish a direct NASP-HSP90 interface, stoichiometry, or functional dependency. The beta assignment is sequence based; the validation antibody was broad HSP90, no alpha comparator was tested, and no NASP or HSP90 perturbation assessed biological function.

The decisive relationship is genetic/functional rather than physical: the article does not assay an NASP-HSP90 complex, and its NASP affinity experiments do not display HSP90. HSP90 beta acts in a broader Hsc70/LAMP2A chaperone-mediated-autophagy model. The alpha negative result is text-only, and missing Supplemental Figure S6 contains specificity and fractionation controls relevant to the proposed mechanism.

C-RAF/RAF1 immunoprecipitation recovered Hsp90, XIAP, and CHIP in a current quality-control complex. XIAP increased Hsp90 recovery with C-RAF, CHIP recruitment, C-RAF ubiquitination, and turnover, while 17-AAG promoted C-RAF loss. These experiments support C-RAF as a broad cytosolic-Hsp90 client whose quality control is modulated by XIAP and CHIP. Protein-specific handling is supported, with remaining model, attribution, or regulatory limitations.

client_assessments.rationale: PMID30536958: The recorded experiments place RARA in chaperone machinery or regulation of HSP90/another substrate; they do not demonstrate that RARA is the chaperoned substrate. Recorded result: The zinc-inducible PML/RARA fusion reduced HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 transcripts and broad HSP90 protein in U937-PR9 cells but not zinc-treated mock controls. In PML/RARA-positive NB4 cells, fusion occupancy was detected at RARE-containing HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 promoter regions; ATRA-mediated loss of the fusion reduced occupancy, increased H3K14 acetylation, and restored HSP90 transcription. This supports a fusion-specific RARA-component upstream transcriptional-regulator relationship for both cytosolic HSP90 isoforms, not an HSP90 client or isolated wild-type RARA mechanism.
limitations: PML and RARA were not perturbed separately; the regulatory activity belongs to the PML/RARA fusion. ATRA is mechanistically aligned with the RARA moiety but also degrades the fusion and activates endogenous retinoid receptors, so its effects alone cannot assign a wild-type RARA relationship. Broad HSP90 immunoblots do not separate alpha from beta protein, although both transcripts and promoter regions are resolved.

To establish candidacy, additional source results would need a controlled protein-specific folding, maturation, maintenance, productive-assembly or competence response linked to HSP90; association, RNA/pathway response or machinery membership alone is insufficient.

summary: Amyloid-beta reduced Hsp90, TERT protein, and telomerase activity in murine cerebral endothelial cells. Combined HSP90-alpha/beta siRNA independently reduced TERT abundance and telomerase activity, while geldanamycin and radicicol potentiated telomerase inhibition and apoptosis. Amyloid-beta increased ubiquitinated TERT, and MG132 restored Hsp90 and TERT abundance together with telomerase activity. TERT siRNA also reduced telomerase activity and increased amyloid toxicity. These current orthogonal perturbations support TERT as a broad cytosolic-Hsp90 client whose stability and enzymatic activity depend on the Hsp90 system in this stress model.
